import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers using t-statistics and effect sizes
    t_stats = []
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] in ('derived', 'expression', 'copy_number', 'clinical'):
            # Calculate Welch's t-test statistic
            group0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            group1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            n0, n1 = len(group0), len(group1)
            if n0 > 1 and n1 > 1:
                var0, var1 = np.var(group0), np.var(group1)
                se = np.sqrt(var0/n0 + var1/n1)
                t = (np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)) / se
                t_stats.append((abs(t), i))
                effect_sizes.append((abs(np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)), i))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic magnitude
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top candidates for drivers
    candidates = [i for _, i in t_stats[:10]]
    drivers = []
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    if len(candidates) > 0:
        corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, candidates].T)
        selected = set()
        for i in range(len(candidates)):
            if i not in selected:
                selected.add(i)
                for j in range(i+1, len(candidates)):
                    if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                        selected.add(j)
        
        # Get actual driver IDs
        driver_ids = [feats.ids[candidates[i]] for i in sorted(selected)]
    else:
        driver_ids = []
    
    # If no strong signals, return empty design
    if not driver_ids or len(driver_ids) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select top drivers by effect size (limit to MAX_DRIVERS)
    driver_effect_sizes = [(abs(np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(d)] ) - 
                               np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(d)])), d) 
                          for d in driver_ids]
    driver_effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    drivers = tuple(d[1] for d in driver_effect_sizes[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(driver_effect_sizes))])
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = tuple(driver_ids)
    products = ()
    
    # Build loadings for weighted score
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(driver_ids):
        # Use standardized coefficients from simple logistic regression
        # as proxy for importance
        x = feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)]
        y = feats.y
        # Simple weighted score using effect size
        mean_diff = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
        loadings[fid] = mean_diff
    
    # Normalize loadings to avoid extreme weights
    if loadings:
        max_abs = max(abs(w) for w in loadings.values())
        if max_abs > 0:
            loadings = {k: v/max_abs for k, v in loadings.items()}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
